tob-10075: Rudolf Steiner, founder of the spiritual movement called Anthroposophy, reinterprets early Christianity as a mystery teaching about inner transformation. He draws parallels between the gospels and the secret rites of ancient Greek and Egyptian cults, arguing that Christ’s story describes a path of spiritual initiation. The book is a key early statement of Steiner’s esoteric worldview.
tob-10175: The prophet Micah preached in the eighth century BC, denouncing the corruption of Jerusalem’s rulers while offering hope to ordinary people. His book contains one of the Bible’s most quoted moral demands: to ‘do justly, and to love mercy, and to walk humbly with thy God.’ Short and direct, it pairs fierce judgment with a promise of a peaceful future under a coming king.
tob-10375: Ralph Shirley’s survey introduces the occultists and mystics of history — astrologers, alchemists, seers, and secret-society founders — from antiquity to his own day. Each chapter sketches a figure or movement, from medieval magicians to Victorian spiritualists. Written for curious general readers, it offers a lively tour of the fringe thinkers who shaped Western esotericism.
tob-14475: Charles Leadbeater’s short Theosophical manual describes the astral plane — the unseen world of feelings and wants that, he claimed, wraps around our own. He explains its sights, its dwellers, and how the dead pass through it. Written for fellow Theosophists, it became a standard guide to the movement’s map of hidden worlds.
tob-4075: The Polish seeker Michael Sendivogius wrote this tract on the makers’ stone in the early 1600s, claiming to draw his light ‘from nature’s own well.’ He pictures the secret fire and the inmost salt of metals in riddling, songlike speech. The work was pored over across Europe by hunters of transmutation.
tob-4146-15475: The second volume of Ganguli’s Mahabharata bears the tale onward — the princes’ outlawry, their woodland years, and the mustering storm of the Kuru war. Through tales within tales the epic teaches right in every hue. The rendering’s steady Victorian prose upholds the poem’s huge weight.
tob-9052-15475: The second volume of Ganguli’s Mahabharata trails the princes into the wilds — forest years, hidings, the slow march toward war. Tales within tales bear the epic’s teaching on right living. The Victorian prose upholds the poem’s grandeur faithfully.
tob-13329-15475: The second volume bears Ganguli’s Mahabharata through the princes’ long outlawry — woodland years, disguisings, and the brewing storm of the Kuru war. Tales within tales teach right in every shade, from kingcraft to godliness. The steady Victorian prose upholds the epic’s vast weight.
cia-0000102975: A May 1983 report on a quiet diplomatic standoff: Koreans stranded on the Soviet island of Sakhalin since World War II, whom Moscow would not discuss with Japan. Tens of thousands had been brought there as wartime laborers and never allowed home. The document shows how Cold War rivalries froze even simple human questions for decades.
cia-0000106275: A November 1965 report on communist road-building in Laos. New roads through the jungle meant faster movement of troops and supplies along the Ho Chi Minh Trail network. The CIA tracked construction as carefully as battles, because in a guerrilla war the shovel could matter as much as the rifle.
cia-0000108075: An October 1966 report, its title carrying the archive's typos, on American and Thai prisoners held near Ban Na Kay in Laos's Houa Phan province. Downed airmen and their allies vanished into the jungle prison system of the secret war. The entry is a fragment of the long effort to account for every missing man.
cia-0000108475: The weekly terrorism situation report for July 23, 1980, summing up seven days of attacks and threats for American officials. Regular as clockwork, these briefings kept terrorism on the agenda even when no single crisis dominated. The document shows routine vigilance — the unglamorous backbone of counterterrorism.
cia-0000119675: An untitled February 1969 statement by John Sweeney — a name that recurs in desertion-related files. Statements like this one were collected, filed, and cross-referenced. The entry is a single voice preserved in the archive, its context scattered across companion documents.
cia-0000124275: A November 1957 report on the announcement of the satellite launching at a Soviet embassy reception — the truncated title cuts off the date. Soviet diplomats toasted Sputnik at cocktail parties while the West reeled. The entry captures triumph as theater: the satellite as a propaganda weapon.
cia-0000126875: An August 1968 survey of Third World reaction to the Soviet invasion of Czechoslovakia. Newly independent nations watched a superpower crush a small country's freedom — and drew conclusions. The document measures the invasion's cost in the court of world opinion.
cia-0000126975: An October 1975 weekly review on Angola after independence. The flag was raised; the war began in earnest. The document surveys a new nation already tearing itself apart — independence day as the starting gun.
cia-0000132275: Situation Report 581: bombs exploding in Lebanon — the truncated title cuts off the context. The Gulf War's shockwaves reached Beirut's endless conflict. The document shows the region's violence syncing up: one war's echo in another's streets.
cia-0000132575: An October 1960 report on the Peru-Ecuador boundary dispute — the archive's spelling says Pru. The old border quarrel flared again, as it did every generation. The document is the Andes' eternal argument: the line on the map, disputed.
cia-0000132675: A 1961 report, its title carrying the archive's typo, on insurgent activity increasing in Cuba. The counterrevolution was growing — the Bay of Pigs approaching. The document is the insurgency, rising: the resistance, arming.
cia-0000134275: A 1959 report: Castro's excesses alienating other Latin American countries. The revolution's style was costing it friends. The document is the alienation: the neighbors, put off.
cia-0000135875: A 1953 program for PBSUCCESS. The operation's program — its phases, its goals. The document is the program: the coup, scheduled.
cia-0000135975: A 1954 cable from LINCOLN reporting detected surveillance of a residence. The watchers were being watched. The document is the counter-surveillance: the watch, spotted.
cia-0000136275: A 1954 cable from LINCOLN on broadcast tape production. The propaganda factory, running. The document is the production: the tapes, made.
cia-0000136375: A 1954 cable from LINCOLN on immediate funding requirements. The money, needed now. The document is the requirement: the funds, urgent.
cia-0000136875: A 1954 cable to the senior representative at LINCOLN on headquarters' concurrence with the LCFLUTTER team's flight plan — the archive's spelling says concurrance. The polygraph team's travel, approved. The entry is the concurrence: the plan, blessed.
cia-0000136975: A 1954 cable to the senior representative at LINCOLN suggesting using up text instead of Molotov's true text — the truncated title cuts off the context. The propaganda edit. The document is the substitution: the text, swapped.
cia-0000141175: A 1969 claim for compensation on account of the death of Juan Gonzalez Romero. The paperwork of loss. The document is the claim: the death, compensated.
un-ga-res-a-69-75: Resolution A/69/75, cataloged with the year 2013 — close to the session but not quite, a small puzzle. The entry preserves the designation and notes the near-miss.
un-ga-res-52-175: Resolution 52/175, adopted in 1998 during the 52nd session — this one aligns. The late-nineties Assembly deciding. The designation and year are certain; the subject is in the text.
un-sc-res-75: Security Council Resolution 75, adopted in 1949. The deliberations rolled on. The number and year survive; the decision lives in the text.
un-sc-res-1375: Security Council Resolution 1375, adopted in 2001 — aligned. The crisis year's Council deliberated. The designation and year survive; the act lives in the text.
un-sc-res-1575: Security Council Resolution 1575, cataloged with the year 2003 — the numbering suggests 2004, a small inconsistency. The designation is kept; the date is questioned.
un-sc-res-1775: Security Council Resolution 1775, adopted in 2007 — aligned. The Council deciding. The designation and year endure; the act is in the text.
cia-0000132775: A 1960 CIA file on Cuban developments, numbered 0000132775. The year's Cuba coverage, thickening. The entry is the thickening: the coverage, deep.
cia-0000139475: A 1986 CIA file: a DCI hostage location task force report, numbered 0000139475. The hostage hunt's paper trail. The document is the trail: the hunt, documented.
frus-1943-cairo-tehran-d75: The President to the Secretary of State, October 30, 1943 — Document 75. The White House answered. The message is the answer: the president, to the department.
frus-1943-cairo-tehran-d175: The President to the Secretary of State, October 30, 1943 — Document 175. A second that day. The message is the doubling: the day, crowded.
frus-1943-cairo-tehran-d275: A memorandum of conversation — the truncated title cuts off the date — Document 275. Another talk, recorded. The memo is the record: the words, kept.
frus-1943-cairo-tehran-d375: Boettiger minutes — the truncated title cuts off the date — Document 375. A third notetaker's record. The minutes are Boettiger's: the talks, triangulated.
arxiv-2605-08775: A few galaxies fire particle jets straight at Earth, and some may be the long-sought sources of high-energy cosmic neutrinos. Hubing Xiao and coauthors continue the hunt in this second paper of the series, modeling the light of candidate blazars across the whole spectrum with a hadronic model in which protons drive the emission. The work narrows the list of neutrino suspects.
arxiv-2605-08975: Fast reactions need fast motion planning: generating trajectories eats latency in real-time systems. Yunseong Jeon, Namcheol Lee, Yoonsu Lee, and colleagues analyze where Alpamayo 1 loses time and optimize it with more efficient trajectory generation. The 2026 paper is latency engineering for a real-time planning system.
arxiv-2605-09275: Diffusion models usually live in flat vector spaces, but tensors carry richer multi-way structure. Jinhua Lyu, Tianmin Yu, Brian Kim, and colleagues diffuse in aligned tensor space with DiffATS. The 2026 paper is generative modeling that respects the richer geometry of tensors.
arxiv-2605-10075: Testing large language models actively — allocating the test budget via approximate Neyman allocation. Zeli Liu, Jiancheng Zhang, Cong Liu, and Yinglun Zhu develop the method. The 2026 paper is LLM evaluation done efficiently. It tests smarter rather than harder, saving budget.
plos-pone-0003375: Facing datasets too big to handle by hand, these 2008 bioinformatics researchers built a fast clustering tool. Metagenomic projects sequence millions of DNA fragments from environments, and grouping near-duplicates is the first hard step. Applied to the Sorcerer II ocean-sampling data, their method grouped enormous datasets quickly, making gene cataloging from such projects practical.
plos-pone-0003475: Statisticians sized up gene-hunting studies for a tricky variation in this 2008 paper. Copy number polymorphisms, stretches of DNA that vary in how many repeats people carry, may shape disease risk, but finding them takes careful planning. The authors calculated the statistical power and sample sizes needed for case-control studies of these variants, with examples showing the math in action.
plos-pone-0003575: Bioinformaticians took inventory of human genetic typos in this 2008 paper. With genome databases swelling, the team catalogued coding-sequence variations and their predicted effects on proteins. The organized catalogue helps researchers separate harmless variants from the ones likely to cause disease.
plos-pone-0003675: In 2009, Oomen, Girardi, and Cahyadi found early neglect hitting male and female brains differently. Rat pups deprived of their mothers showed opposite changes in the birth of new brain cells by sex. The split result offers a clue to why depression, tied to this brain growth, strikes women more than men.
plos-pone-0003775: Fernando, Karishma, and Szathmáry proposed brains that copy themselves in this 2008 paper. Their mechanism for duplicating neuronal network topology suggests how the brain might perform causal inference and copy functions. The idea gives neuroscience a concrete model for learning by internal copying.
plos-pone-0003875: Working in 2008, Young, Norman, and Humphreys showed words reshaping sickness. Medical language changed how the public perceived newly medicalized conditions. The study reveals terminology itself as a force in how societies understand illness.
plos-pone-0003975: In 2008, Rits, van Dort, and Kootstra tied HIV risk to a gene's control region. Variants near the cyclophilin A gene tracked with who caught HIV-1 and how fast it progressed. The regulatory DNA, not the protein code, made the difference in susceptibility. The result shows tiny control-region changes shaping who the epidemic hits hardest.
plos-pone-0004075: In 2008, Cummings, Bednarski, and Maizels linked two kinds of heredity at last. Epigenetic marks on DNA spurred new genetic variation. The marks nudged repair machinery toward shuffling the genome. The bold finding blurs the line between soft and hard inheritance.
plos-pone-0004175: In 2009, Urbach and Benvenisty modeled a mostly lethal chromosome loss. Human embryonic stem cells stood in for 45,XO Turner syndrome embryos. Most XO conceptions are lost early; the model shows why. The stem-cell window opens study of early lethality at last.
plos-pone-0004275: In 2009, Kang, Choi, and Lee measured blood flow with light and math. Spatiotemporal analysis of molecular dynamics mapped peripheral tissue perfusion. The light-based method tracked flow without surgery. The tool aids leg diagnosis. The approach could guide treatment of blocked limbs.
plos-pone-0358775: A simple colored tape around a child’s upper arm can detect malnutrition early — and families themselves can use it. This study examines whether parents find family-led arm-circumference screening acceptable, doable, and affordable. The results show how a low-tech tool placed in mothers’ hands could catch hungry children before they ever reach a clinic.
plos-pone-0352575: In cold-region open-pit coal mines, waste dumps can slide — and temperature, moisture, and rain decide when. This paper analyzed how those three factors affect internal dump slope stability, validated with drainage data. The findings give mine engineers concrete rules for keeping waste slopes standing.
plos-pone-0358075: Ancient rock carvers chose their stone carefully — and this paper argues the depth of their carvings reveals geological know-how. Analyzing carving depth against rock properties, the study suggests carvers read the stone’s character, choosing depth to suit hardness and grain. The finding credits ancient artisans with practical geology.
plos-pone-0358575: How nurses talk to patients shapes healing — but measuring it needs a valid scale. This paper tested the psychometric features of the Patient-Centered Communication Scale among Iranian clinical nurses. The validation shows whether the tool truly captures communication quality in this setting.
plos-pone-0358475: Diabetes is striking younger — and the global numbers are stark. This analysis of the Global Burden of Disease Study 2023 tracked diabetes burdens in adolescents from 1990 to 2023, with future trend predictions. The trajectories warn health systems everywhere about what is coming their way.
plos-pone-0357975: AI reading breast ultrasounds could speed up cancer assessment pathways. This multi-site observational evaluation tested Breast AI–supported ultrasound risk stratification in real clinical pathways. The real-world evaluation shows whether the AI helps clinics sort patient risk accurately outside the lab.
plos-pone-0357375: Anxiety keeps women away from mammograms — with potentially deadly consequences. This study measured the impact of anxiety and affective disorders on breast cancer screening among women in Puerto Rico. The findings prove that mental health is a screening barrier too, one that outreach programs must address directly.
plos-pone-0355675: Preventing depression in primary care works best when it’s personal. The e-predictD pilot study combined qualitative and quantitative findings toward personalized prevention interventions. The mixed-methods results guide how to tailor depression prevention to each patient’s risk profile and life context.
plos-pone-0356875: Semiarid northern Pakistan needs wheat that yields reliably under water stress. This paper evaluated high-performing hybrid wheat lines to unlock yield potential in those harsh conditions. The winning lines point the way toward greater food security for one of the region’s most vulnerable farming zones.
plos-pone-0358275: Workplace noise may harm the liver — especially in heavier workers. This cross-sectional study found body mass index modifies the association between occupational noise exposure duration and ultrasound-detected hepatic steatosis. The interaction suggests noise acts as a metabolic stressor too, not merely a hearing hazard.
plos-pone-0355975: ILF3 is a newly recognized regulator of red blood cell formation. This single-cell transcriptomic analysis, backed by cellular experiments, mapped ILF3’s role in erythroid differentiation. The gene joins the regulatory cast directing how stem cells become the oxygen-carrying red cells we depend on.
plos-pone-0357575: Some emergency department patients bounce back within a day of discharge — often sicker. This paper developed and internally validated a simple risk stratification score for unplanned ED revisits within 24 hours. The score flags high-risk patients for closer follow-up before they leave.
plos-pone-0357275: Social isolation quietly erodes the intrinsic capacity of older Hispanic adults in the United States. This study explored those associations across geographic and social contexts. The findings guide culturally attuned support — recognizing that isolation lands differently in different communities.
plos-pone-0356475: Groundwater quality in the main urban area of Bozho needed rigorous evaluation. This case study constructed and applied connection number and projection pursuit models for that assessment. The models give water managers a structured, quantitative picture of their aquifer’s health.
plos-pone-0355375: Can yoga — mindful or conventional — help teenagers regulate their emotions? This nonrandomized quasi-experimental study tested a Mindful Yoga intervention against Common Yoga on adolescents’ emotion regulation and well-being. The comparison reveals whether the mindfulness ingredient adds real value.
plos-pone-0356775: Basketball demands explosive curved sprints — and the mechanics matter. This paper assessed curvilinear sprint performance, examining the roles of stretch-shortening cycle function and isometric force-time metrics. The findings tell strength coaches precisely which physical qualities to train for game-speed agility.
plos-pone-0354875: Hate speech in Roman Urdu — Urdu written in Latin script — evades most detection tools. LEXF-ATT-XLM is a hybrid lexicon-enhanced attention model built for this low-resource language. The specialized model brings hate speech detection to millions of speakers the big platforms overlook.
plos-pone-0351775: Not all ecological impacts of invasive species weigh equally — but whose judgment counts? This paper surveyed expert perceptions of the relative importance of different ecological impacts of biological invasions. The structured expert judgment helps managers prioritize among the many harms invaders inflict.
plos-pone-0350075: Parkrunners chase personal bests — sometimes into injury. This study associated training behaviors with injuries in performance-oriented parkrunners, using both traditional statistics and machine learning. The dual analysis reveals which training patterns break runners — and whether AI spots risks that classic stats miss.
plos-pone-0356175: Speeding up braces with surgery sounds appealing — unless it dissolves tooth roots. This harms-focused systematic review asked whether invasive surgical acceleration of orthodontic tooth movement increases root resorption. The safety-first synthesis gives orthodontists and patients the risk data that efficacy studies gloss over.
plos-pone-0356375: Smart microgrids need protection systems that adapt when faults strike. This paper developed adaptive and resilient protection coordination enabled by a directional fault current limiter. The intelligent protection keeps the lights on through faults that would black out conventionally protected grids.
plos-pone-0356275: A year before a mild cognitive impairment diagnosis, many older adults are already on risky drug regimens. This paper measured the one-year pre-diagnostic prevalence of polypharmacy and potentially inappropriate medication use in community-dwelling adults. The findings flag a window where deprescribing might slow cognitive decline.
plos-pone-0349175: Tunnel cracks and water leaks threaten infrastructure — and AI can map them. This paper applied a TransUNet framework for semantic segmentation and quantitative analysis of tunnel cracks and leakage. The automated inspection promises safer tunnels through earlier, more precise defect detection.
plos-pone-0355475: Milk protein-coated medium-chain triglycerides might nudge the body toward ketosis gently. This randomized, double-blind, crossover study tested their ketogenic effects in healthy men. The findings reveal whether this palatable formulation can deliver ketone benefits without the harsh keto diet.
plos-pone-0355275: Wild meat — bushmeat — carries zoonotic disease risks shaped by culture and behavior. This paper examined the cultural and behavioral drivers of that risk along the value chain in rural Cameroon. The findings show that spillover prevention must work with local practices, not against them.
plos-pone-0352675: Emotions about health topics spread digitally — and rumor refutation reshapes the contagion. This paper explored those contagion routes through multidimensional configuration analysis before and after refutation. The findings reveal how corrections do — and don’t — calm emotional wildfires online.
europmc-pmc2819875: Long before Zika made global headlines, this 2009 paper warned it was on the move. The author reviews evidence of Zika virus spreading outside Africa, its original range. The short report flagged an emerging pathogen early. Years later, when Zika exploded across the Americas, this paper read like a prescient alarm.
europmc-pmc2854775: The afterbirth guards the womb, but can it stop specks? This 2010 study probes how much nano-sized stuff the human placenta lets through. The team ran beads across real placentas. Their read showed the guard leaks more than hoped, a flag for safer goods for moms.
europmc-pmc2944075: Mercury poisoning in inland China comes from rice, not fish. This 2010 paper shows rice, rather than fish, is the major pathway for methylmercury exposure in inland China. The authors trace the toxin from mines to paddies to plates. Their finding rewrote mercury risk maps for the region.
europmc-pmc2981575: Long stretches of matching DNA record family history. This 2010 paper shows runs of homozygosity trace population history and cousin marriage. The authors read the patterns in genomes. Their work aids ancestry and disease gene hunts. Island peoples carry the longest such stretches.
europmc-pmc3048375: Rare gene variants need sharp tests. This 2011 paper offers a test for oddball distributions of rare variants. The authors' method spots the strange patterns. Their tool aided gene hunting. The test handles thousands of variants at once. Gene hunters still use it for rare diseases.
europmc-pmc3063175: Depression may age cells faster. This 2011 paper links shorter chromosome caps in depression to illness length and stress. The authors' early findings intrigue psychiatrists. Their work bridges mind and body. Long episodes wore the caps shortest. Exercise might slow the wearing, they suggest.
europmc-pmc3068975: Test-accuracy curves got an open toolkit. This 2011 paper brings pROC, an R package for drawing and comparing ROC curves. The authors' tool became a diagnostics staple. Their software spread through labs. Thousands of papers plot with it. Smooth curves beat jagged ones for reading.
europmc-pmc3071375: Cells got a tag for two microscopes at once. This 2011 paper builds a gene-encoded tag that glows for light microscopes and stains for electron ones. The authors bridge both scales. Their tool spread through labs. One tag now serves both imaging worlds.
europmc-pmc3081075: Failing eye nerves got a power-plant review. This 2011 paper covers mitochondrial optic nerve diseases and their treatments. The authors survey causes and emerging cures. Their overview guides eye doctors. LHON families gained the most hope. Gene therapy trials are now underway.
europmc-pmc3084475: Hospital patients go hungry too often. This 2011 review tallies how many inpatients are malnourished and what it costs. The authors demand routine screening. Their work shaped nutrition care. A third of patients arrive undernourished. Screened wards discharge patients sooner. The review is now taught in nursing schools.
europmc-pmc6510875: Tumors do not grow in isolation - the nutrients around them decide how fast cancer cells multiply. This study measured the actual chemical mix surrounding mouse tumors to see which food sources are available. Knowing what tumors eat helps scientists design better lab experiments and, eventually, treatments that starve cancer of the nutrients it needs most.
europmc-pmc6529775: Sepsis can stun the heart, and scientists are tracing the molecular chain of blame. In mice given bacterial toxin, a sensor pathway called STING-IRF3 switched on inflammation, heart-cell suicide, and a fiery cell death called pyroptosis - together driving cardiac failure. Blocking this pathway eased the damage, nominating it as a treatment target for sepsis-induced heart injury.
europmc-pmc6534875: A tumor biopsy contains a stew of cancer and immune cells, and knowing the mix matters for immunotherapy. The authors built quanTIseq, a computational method that unmixes bulk RNA-sequencing data into fractions of ten immune cell types. Validated against lab measurements and applied to 8,000 tumors, it lets researchers read the immune landscape of cancer from sequencing data alone.
europmc-pmc6540575: A tiny chemical tag - a methyl group on adenine, called m6A - decorates messenger RNAs and controls their fate. In cancer, the enzymes that add, read, and erase m6A go awry, reshaping which genes stay active. This review maps m6A's roles across human tumors, presenting the modification machinery as both a window into cancer biology and a target for new drugs.
europmc-pmc6550175: Hospital records hold clues for predicting who gets sick - but turning messy EHR data into forecasts usually takes heavy manual work. This 2018 study showed deep learning can scale: neural networks trained directly on raw electronic health records predicted outcomes like readmission and mortality. The work made the case that AI can read charts and warn doctors earlier.
europmc-pmc6600375: TGF-beta is a master signal that tells cells when to grow, move, or change identity - and cancers hijack it to spread. This review traces how the cytokine drives epithelial-mesenchymal transition, the shape-shift that lets tumor cells break away and metastasize. Blocking this hijacked signal could keep cancers pinned in place.
europmc-pmc6603175: Hyaluronic acid - the goo that cushions joints and plumps skin - does far more than fill space. This review traces its molecular tricks: how the giant sugar chains signal cells, calm inflammation, and guide healing. From arthritis shots to wound care, the molecule's therapeutic road keeps widening.
europmc-pmc6607375: When new viruses emerge, labs must share genetic data fast - but credit and control worries slow them down. GISAID cracked the dilemma with a sharing platform that protects contributors' rights while speeding access. This account of its innovative model shows how data diplomacy helped the world track flu and other threats.
europmc-pmc6639075: Single-cell RNA sequencing can now read each cell's active gene program - but turning reads into meaning takes work. This paper presents methods for pulling out the expression programs behind cell identity and cell activity. The tools help biologists map who cells are and what they are doing.
europmc-pmc6701375: Huntington's timing has long been blamed on the length of a stuttering CAG repeat - but the real culprit is subtler. This consortium study shows the uninterrupted repeat sequence itself, not the polyglutamine tract length, sets the disease clock. The finding rewrites the genetics of onset.
europmc-pmc6728375: Western diets rich in omega-6 fats fatten mice - unless their gut microbes intervene. This study shows microbiota protect against obesity by converting dietary polyunsaturated fatty acids into beneficial metabolites. The microbes, not just the menu, decide what fat does to the body.
gao-gaoreports-gao-07-875: Detainees could not get a dial tone in 2007 — GAO's report finds phone-access failures rampant in immigration lockups, plus other shortfalls. The findings document a detention system failing its own standards. The report argues that locked up should not mean cut off.
gao-gaoreports-b-299175: Geo-Seis Helicopters doubled its March 2007 protest — two case numbers, one aviation fight — and GAO's combined ruling settles both claims at once. The firm challenged the awards, and the call weighs each claim. Paired filings get one careful answer. Two dockets, one fair verdict.
gao-gaoreports-gao-07-375: The 9/11 wounds were still open in 2007, and GAO's report says progress had been made on the vulnerabilities, though federal action had to continue. The findings balance credit and warning. The report argues that the lessons of the towers could not be filed away. The vigilance had to outlast the memory.
gao-gaoreports-b-298975: Stewart Distributors took its January 2007 contract fight to GAO, and this ruling is the verdict on the claims. The firm said the agency's award was unfair, and the call tests the protest. Distribution deals get the same full hearing as the rest.
openalex-w7212003675: Leprosy still spreads in parts of Brazil despite being curable. This paper studies case data from Uberlandia, a city in Minas Gerais, between 2018 and 2022, a period that includes the COVID-19 pandemic. The authors trace infection patterns and propose practical prevention and control steps the city could take. It doubles as a local health report and a playbook for fighting a neglected disease.
openalex-w7204225575: When hackers strike critical infrastructure, investigators face both technical puzzles and legal mazes. This article studies the clash between computer forensics and criminal-law interpretation in cyberattacks on essential systems, using a massive service outage as a case study. The authors probe how courts should read digital evidence. A dense but important study of law catching up with code.
openalex-w7117325475: Inside the magnet LaMnSi, tiny atomic magnets line up in a strict pattern. This lab paper nailed down that pattern using magnetic resonance scans of manganese and lanthanum atoms. The team mapped how the spins point and how electrons behave. A close-up study of order in a quantum crystal.
pmc-13462675: A 2026 clinical study finding that COVID-19 patients with autoimmune disease who received B-cell depleting therapy — drugs that wipe out antibody-making cells — shed the virus longer than those on TNF inhibitors. Prolonged shedding means a longer infectious window. The comparison helps doctors weigh infection risk when choosing autoimmune treatments during outbreaks.
pmc-13454375: In this 2026 allergy study from a subarctic region, researchers tracked how exposure to birch rust spores — fungal spores from diseased birch trees — lined up with upper airway symptoms. The pattern suggests a previously unrecognized seasonal allergen. For northern communities, naming the trigger is the first step toward relief.
pmc-13448775: In this 2026 study, researchers tested whether the waist-to-BMI ratio predicts musculoskeletal disease in people with type 2 diabetes, combining cohort data with PhIP-Seq antibody profiling. Body-fat distribution may matter more than total weight for joint and muscle risk. The dual approach links a simple measure to immune signatures.
pmc-13430975: This 2026 study found that chronic smoking impairs the glymphatic system — the brain's waste-clearance plumbing — and cognition in adolescent mice, acting through heart, blood vessel, and aquaporin-4 water-channel mechanisms around vessels. Smoking harms the teenage brain through the body, not just the lungs. The multi-organ chain is the key insight.
pmc-13387175: In this 2026 toxicology paper, nano-formulated rosmarinic acid — from rosemary — protected against chlorfenapyr pesticide-induced testicular toxicity by modulating NRF2/HO-1 and NF-κB/NLRP3 signaling pathways. The antioxidant and anti-inflammatory action preserved reproductive tissue. The study tests a natural compound against an agricultural toxin.
pmc-13387075: A 2026 toxicology paper showing that the amino acid serine ameliorates cadmium-induced testicular injury by regulating the PGAM1/PHGDH signaling pathway. Cadmium is a widespread environmental toxin, and serine's protective effect runs through metabolic reprogramming. The finding suggests a simple nutritional intervention.
pmc-13429875: A 2026 prospective cohort study of obstetric outcomes after IVF/ICSI in women with endometriosis or adenomyosis diagnosed by ultrasound. Fertility treatment in these patients carries distinct risks. The cohort data quantify them.
pmc-13440675: A 2026 neuropathology paper finding Alzheimer's changes, alpha-synuclein, and TDP-43 expression in the brains of children and young adults from a polluted city (the title is truncated). Early pathology in young brains is alarming. The environmental link demands attention.
pmc-13424875: A 2026 sociology paper on life course trajectory segregation and political polarization in contemporary Sweden. Where life takes you shapes how you vote. The segregation finding is the insight.
pmc-13599775: A 2026 study of depression trends in Europe and their sociodemographic differences. Who gets depressed is shifting. The trends inform mental health policy.
